1.word_for_word: पञ्चत्रिंशे वनं याते कृष्णे गोकुल-योषितः । — At the age of thirty-five, when Lord Kṛṣṇa went to the forest, the women of Gokula visited Him.; युग्म-श्लोकानुगीतेन निन्युर् दुःखेन वासरान् ॥ — They spent their days in misery singing a pair of verses.; एवं रात्रिषु श्री-कृष्णेन स्वैरम् अभिरमितानां दिवा तद्-विरहितानां गोपीनाम् अनुगीतेन दिन-निस्तार-प्रकारम् आह---गोप्य इति । — Thus, by following the songs of the gopīs, who were freely enjoyed by Lord Kṛṣṇa at night and who were separated from Him during the day, he described the manner of saving the day by saying, “Gopīs.”; दुःखेन कृच्छ्रेण ॥१॥ — with pain and difficulty.
1.translation: At the age of thirty-five, when Lord Kṛṣṇa went to the forest, the women of Gokula visited Him. They spent their days in misery singing a pair of verses. Thus, by following the songs of the gopīs, who were freely enjoyed by Lord Kṛṣṇa at night and who were separated from Him during the day, he described the manner of saving the day by saying, “Gopīs.” with pain and difficulty.

2-3.word_for_word: वाम-बाहु-कृत-वाम-कपोल इत्य्-आदीनि द्वादश-युगलानि । — There are twelve pairs of left-arm, left-handed, and left-handed cheeks.; हे गोप्यः ! — O Gopis!; वाम-बाहौ तन्-मूले कृतोऽर्पितः वामः कपोलो येन सः । — The left arm is the one whose left forehead is placed at the root of the tree.; वल्गिते नर्तिते भ्रुवौ यस्य येन वा स वल्गित-भ्रूर् मुकुन्दः अधरेऽर्पितं वेणुं कोमलाङ्गुलीभिर् आश्रिता मार्गाः सप्त-स्वर-च्छिद्राणि यस्य तं, — He whose eyebrows are waving and dancing, or whose eyebrows are waving, Mukunda, whose lips are offered to the flute, whose paths are supported by tender fingers, and whose holes are seven notes,; यत्र यदा ईरयति वादयति तदा व्योम-यानानां सिद्धानां वनिताः सिद्धैः स्व-पतिभिः सह वर्तमाना अपि तत् वेण्व्-ईरणम् उपधार्य आकर्ण्य प्रथमं विस्मिताः ततः काम-मार्गणेभ्यः समर्पिताणि चित्तानि याभिस् ताः, तत् पर-वशा इत्य् अर्थः । — Where, whenever he plays the iera, the wives of the Siddhas of the celestial beings, even though they are with their Siddha husbands, are first astonished to hear it, and then their minds are devoted to the pursuit of lust, which means that it is under the control of others.; सलज्जाः सत्यः कश्मलं मोहं ययुः । — They were shy, truthful, tired and deluded.; अत्र लिङ्गम् अपस्मृता विस्मृता नीव्यो याभिर् इति । — Here the gender is forgotten by those who have forgotten the lowliness.; अत एवं-भूतस्य श्री-कृष्णस्य विरहं कथं सहाम ? — So how can we bear the separation of such-being Sri Krishna?; इति सर्वत्र वाक्य-शेषः ॥२-३॥ — This is the rest of the sentence everywhere.2-3
2-3.translation: There are twelve pairs of left-arm, left-handed, and left-handed cheeks. O Gopis! The left arm is the one whose left forehead is placed at the root of the tree. He whose eyebrows are waving and dancing, or whose eyebrows are waving, Mukunda, whose lips are offered to the flute, whose paths are supported by tender fingers, and whose holes are seven notes, Where, whenever he plays the iera, the wives of the Siddhas of the celestial beings, even though they are with their Siddha husbands, are first astonished to hear it, and then their minds are devoted to the pursuit of lust, which means that it is under the control of others. They were shy, truthful, tired and deluded. Here the gender is forgotten by those who have forgotten the lowliness. So how can we bear the separation of such-being Sri Krishna? This is the rest of the sentence everywhere.2-3

4-5.word_for_word: हन्त हे अबलाः ! — Oh, you weaklings!; इदं चित्रं शृणुत । — Listen to this picture.; हार-हासो हारवद् विशदो हासो यस्य सः । — A necklace-smile is one whose smile is as sharp as a necklace.; यद् वा, वेणु-वादनेनाधो-वदनेन हसतो हारेषु स्फुरन् हास्यो यस्य सः । — Or rather, he whose smile glitters in his necklaces as he laughs with his face downwards as he plays the flute.; यद् वा, हारवद् वक्षसि शोभमानो हास्यो यस्य सः । — Or rather, he whose smile adorns his chest like a necklace.; यद् वा, हाराणां हास इव विशदा स्फूर्तिर् यस्मिन् । — Or rather, in which there is a vivid vibrancy like the smile of a necklace.; उरसीति उरसि स्थिरा विद्युद् इव लक्ष्मीर् यस्य सः । — The chest is the one whose chest is as steady as lightning.; यर्हि यदा कूजित-वेणुर् नादित-वेणुर् भवति, तदा व्रजे वृषा मृगा गावश् च वेणु-वाद्येन हृतानि चेतांसि येषां ते । — Whenever the whistling flute becomes a sounding flute, the bulls, deer and cows in Vraja are those whose minds are captivated by the playing of the flute.; आरात् दूराद् एव दन्तैर् दष्टाः कवला ग्रासा यैः, ते धृता उत्तम्भिताः कर्णा यैस् ते निद्रिता इव लिखितं चित्रम् इव चासन् । — They were bitten by their teeth from a distance from the beginning, their ears were raised, and they looked like a painting written as if they were asleep.; अविदुषाम् तिरश्चाम् इदम् अतिचित्रम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥४-५॥ — This means that it is very strange for the ignorant and the slanted.4-5
4-5.translation: Oh, you weaklings! Listen to this picture. A necklace-smile is one whose smile is as sharp as a necklace. Or rather, he whose smile glitters in his necklaces as he laughs with his face downwards as he plays the flute. Or rather, he whose smile adorns his chest like a necklace. Or rather, in which there is a vivid vibrancy like the smile of a necklace. The chest is the one whose chest is as steady as lightning. Whenever the whistling flute becomes a sounding flute, the bulls, deer and cows in Vraja are those whose minds are captivated by the playing of the flute. They were bitten by their teeth from a distance from the beginning, their ears were raised, and they looked like a painting written as if they were asleep. This means that it is very strange for the ignorant and the slanted.4-5

6-7.word_for_word: अचेतनासु सरित्सु तद् अतीव चित्रम् इत्य् आहुः---हे आलि हे सखि ! — They say that it is very strange in the unconscious rivers: O Ali, O friend!; बर्हिणो मयूरस्य स्तवकाः पुच्छानि धातुर् गैरिक-रागः पलाशानि पल्लवास् तैर् बद्धश् चासौ मल्लानां परिबर्हः परिकरस् तं विडम्बयति अनुकरोति तथा स मुकुन्दः गोपैः सह वेणुनेत्य् उपरितनम् अत्रापि ज्ञातव्यं यत्र यदा गाः समाह्वयति । — The peacock’s peacock’s staves are the tails of the metallic gairika, the lotuses are the leaves, and the wrestlers’ clothing is imitating him, and the Mukunda is playing the flute with the cows.; तर्हि तद्-ध्वनि-श्रवणात् अनिलेन नीतं तस्य पदाम्बुज-रजः स्पृहयन्त्य इव भग्न-गतयः सरितो वै निश्चितं वयम् इव ता अप्य् अबहु-पुण्या यतो न प्राप्नुवन्ति । — Then, when they hear the sound of the Lord, they seem to long for the dust of His lotus feet carried by the wind.; केवलं प्रेम्णा वेपिताः कम्पिताः भुजास् तरङ्गा यासां ताः स्तिमिता निश्चला अपो यासां ता गोप्योऽपि लोचनयोः स्तिमित-जला भवन्ति ॥६-७॥ — The waves of those whose arms are shaken by love alone are still and the waters are still and even the gopīs have stilled tears in their eyes (6-7).
6-7.translation: They say that it is very strange in the unconscious rivers: O Ali, O friend! The peacock’s peacock’s staves are the tails of the metallic gairika, the lotuses are the leaves, and the wrestlers’ clothing is imitating him, and the Mukunda is playing the flute with the cows. Then, when they hear the sound of the Lord, they seem to long for the dust of His lotus feet carried by the wind. The waves of those whose arms are shaken by love alone are still and the waters are still and even the gopīs have stilled tears in their eyes (6-7).

8-9.word_for_word: स्थावरेष्व् अप्य् अतिचित्रं दृश्यत इत्य् आहुः---अनुचरैर् गोपैर् देवैर् वा मुग्धानां वाक्यम् आदि-पुरुष इवेति अचल-भूतिर् निश्चल-श्रीः । — It is said that even in the immovable things it appears very strange.; वेणुना तत्-तन्-नाम्नां गानेन । — By singing those names on the flute.; तदा प्रणता भारेण विटपाः शाखा यासां ताः वन-गता लता स्वस्मिन् विष्णुं प्रकाशमानं सूचयन्त्य इव मधु-धारा ववृषुः स्मेति विस्मये तरवश् च तथा तत्-पतीनाम् अपि तथैवानन्द इति भावः । — Then the branches of the trees, whose branches were bowed down under their weight, showered streams of honey as if indicating that Lord Viṣṇu was shining in them.; एतानि विष्णु-भक्ति-लक्षणानि ॥८-९॥ — These are the characteristics of devotion to Vishnu.8-9
8-9.translation: It is said that even in the immovable things it appears very strange. By singing those names on the flute. Then the branches of the trees, whose branches were bowed down under their weight, showered streams of honey as if indicating that Lord Viṣṇu was shining in them. These are the characteristics of devotion to Vishnu.8-9

10-11.word_for_word: किं च सरसि कमल-वनेषु विहरतां पक्षिणाम् अप्य् आकर्षणं तद् गीतं किं पुनर् अन्येषाम् इत्य् आहुः । — What is more, it is said that the song attracts even the birds that fly in the lotus forests of the lake, what about others?; दर्शनीय-तिलक इति दर्शनीयस् तिलको यस्य सः । — Darshani-tilak is the one whose tilak is visible.; दर्शनीयानां सुन्दराणां मध्ये मुख्य इति वा वन-मालासु या दिव्य-गन्धा तुलसी तस्या मधुना मत्तैर् अलि-कुलैः अलघु उच्चैर् अभीष्टम् अनुकूलं गीतम् आदिर्यन् आदरेण गृह्णन् यर्हि अधरे सन्धित-वेणुर् भवति तर्हि सरसि-सारसा-हंसाः । — The chief among the beautiful things to be seen, or the divine fragrance of the basil, which is in the garlands of the forest, is drunk with its honey, and the swans of the lake, the swans of the lake, take it with respect.; अन्ये च विहङ्गाः चारुना गीतेन हृत-चेतस एत्य् आगत्य हरिम् उपासत अभजन्त तत्-समीपे उपविविशुर् वा हन्तेति विषादे ॥१०-११॥ — Other birds, captivated by the beautiful song, came and worshiped the Lord Hari and worshiped Him or sat down near Him in despair thinking that He was killing them.
10-11.translation: What is more, it is said that the song attracts even the birds that fly in the lotus forests of the lake, what about others? Darshani-tilak is the one whose tilak is visible. The chief among the beautiful things to be seen, or the divine fragrance of the basil, which is in the garlands of the forest, is drunk with its honey, and the swans of the lake, the swans of the lake, take it with respect. Other birds, captivated by the beautiful song, came and worshiped the Lord Hari and worshiped Him or sat down near Him in despair thinking that He was killing them.

12-13.word_for_word: मेघोऽपि हरिं दृष्ट्वा सेवते इत्य् आहुः सह-बल इति । — It is said that even a cloud sees the Supreme Personality of Godhead and serves Him.; हे व्रज-देव्यो गोप्यः सह-बलः सह-रामः श्री-कृष्णः स्रग्भिर् निर्मिताभ्याम् अवतंसाभ्यां कर्ण-भूषणाभ्यां विलासो यस्य सः । — O goddesses of Vraja, gopīs, with your strength, with Rāma, with Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose luxury is the earrings made of garlands made of avatansa.; यद् वा, मुक्ता-फल-स्रग्-आपीडेन विलासो यस्य सः । — Or, rather, the luxury of pearls, fruits, garlands and appeals.; क्षिति-भृतः सानुषु गिरेस् तटेषु वर्तमानः स्वयं जात-हर्षो विश्वं हर्षयन् यदा वेणु-रवेण उपरम्भति निनादयति नादेनापूरयतीत्य् अर्थः । — This means that the earth-bearer, who is present on the slopes and banks of the mountains, is himself born of joy, and when he begins with the sound of his flute, he resounds and fills the world with sound.; तदा मेघो महतः श्री-कृष्णस्यातिक्रमेण शङ्कितं चेतो यस्य सः । — At that time the cloud was the one whose mind was suspicious of the transgression of the great Lord Kṛṣṇa.; न पुनर् अन्यतो याति न चोच्चैर् गर्जति किन्तु तत्रैव स्थितः सन् वेणु-रवम् अनु मन्द-मन्दं गर्जतीति । — He doesn’t go anywhere else and doesn’t roar loudly but stays there and roars slowly to the sound of the flute.; किं च, विश्वार्ति-हरण-साम्यात् सुहृदं श्री-कृष्णं सुमनोभिर् अभ्यवर्षत् । — What’s more, she showered flowers on her friend, Lord Kṛṣṇa, who was equal to removing all suffering.; अदृश्यैर् देवैः क्रियमाणं कुसुम-वर्षं मेघं कल्पयित्वोक्तस् तुषारो वा कुसुमतया कल्पितः । — The rain of flowers caused by the invisible gods is said to be a cloud or snow is said to be a flower.; स एव वा देवता-रूपोऽभ्यवर्षद् इति । — Or that he himself, in the form of a deity, rained down.; प्रतपाद् आतपात् त्रायत इति प्रतपत्रं छत्रं तच्-छायया कुर्वन्न् इति ॥१२.१३॥ — They made an umbrella under the shade of the umbrella, saying that it protected them from the heat of the sun.
12-13.translation: It is said that even a cloud sees the Supreme Personality of Godhead and serves Him. O goddesses of Vraja, gopīs, with your strength, with Rāma, with Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose luxury is the earrings made of garlands made of avatansa. Or, rather, the luxury of pearls, fruits, garlands and appeals. This means that the earth-bearer, who is present on the slopes and banks of the mountains, is himself born of joy, and when he begins with the sound of his flute, he resounds and fills the world with sound. At that time the cloud was the one whose mind was suspicious of the transgression of the great Lord Kṛṣṇa. He doesn’t go anywhere else and doesn’t roar loudly but stays there and roars slowly to the sound of the flute. What’s more, she showered flowers on her friend, Lord Kṛṣṇa, who was equal to removing all suffering. The rain of flowers caused by the invisible gods is said to be a cloud or snow is said to be a flower. Or that he himself, in the form of a deity, rained down. They made an umbrella under the shade of the umbrella, saying that it protected them from the heat of the sun.

14-15.word_for_word: किं च, महद् एतद् आश्चर्यम् इत्य् आहुः--विविधेति । — Moreover, they say that this is a great wonder, and that it is various.; हे सति यशोदे ! — O Sati Yashoda!; तव सुतः नाना-गोप-क्रीडासु निपुणो वेणु-वाद्य-विषये निजैव शिक्षा यासु, ताः स्वोत्प्रेक्षिताः, न त्व् अन्यतः श्रुता इत्य् अर्थः । — This means that your son is skilled in various cow games and that he has learned his own teachings about playing the flute and that he has observed them himself and has not heard them from anyone else.; स्वर-जातीः निषाद-र्षभादि-स्वरालाप-भेदान् अनयत् उन्नीतवान् यदा, तदा सुरेशाः तत् ताः स्वर-जातीः सवनशः मन्त्र-मध्य-तार-भेदेन यतो पीत-ध्वनिर् आगतः, तत आनता कन्धरा चित्तं च येषां, ते उपधार्य सम्यग् आकर्ण्य कवयः कोविदा अपि, — When he brought and raised the differences of vowels, such as the Nishad and the bull, then Suresh, by the difference of the mantra and the middle string, from which the yellow sound came, and whose shoulders and minds he brought,; तेन निश्चितं तत्त्वं तद्-भेदो यैः कश्मलं मोहं ययुः ॥१४-१५॥ — Therefore the truth is certain and the difference between it and those who have gone into fatigue and delusion (14-15).
14-15.translation: Moreover, they say that this is a great wonder, and that it is various. O Sati Yashoda! This means that your son is skilled in various cow games and that he has learned his own teachings about playing the flute and that he has observed them himself and has not heard them from anyone else. When he brought and raised the differences of vowels, such as the Nishad and the bull, then Suresh, by the difference of the mantra and the middle string, from which the yellow sound came, and whose shoulders and minds he brought, Therefore the truth is certain and the difference between it and those who have gone into fatigue and delusion (14-15).

16-17.word_for_word: अस्माकं तु मोहं किं ब्रूमः ? — What about our delusion?; इत्य् आहुः---निज-पदाब्ज-दलैर् इति । — They say that it is by the teams of their own lotus feet.; ध्वजादीनि विचित्राणि ललामानि चिह्नानि येषां तैः, निजानि पदान्य् एवाब्ज-दलानि तैः, व्रज-भुवः खुर-तोदं खुराक्रमण-व्यथां शमयन् वर्ष्मणा देहेन धुर्यो गजस् तद्वद् गतिर् यस्य स कृष्नो वादित-वेणुः सन् यद् व्रजति, — They have flags and other strange red marks, their own feet are like lotus petals, the Vraja-bhuvas, relieving the pain of hooves and hooves, and whose movements are like those of an elephant, whose body is driven by rain,; तेन निमित्तेन स-विलास-वीक्षणेनार्पितो मनो-भव-वेगो यासु ता वयम् । — We are the ones in whom the speed of mind and being is offered by that occasion, by the luxurious gaze.; कुजा वृक्षास् तेषां गतिं गमिताः सत्यो [कश्मलेन] मोहेन न विदामः कबरं वा वसनं वा इति ॥१६.१७॥ — The trees of Kuja have lost their destination out of truth [exhaustion] and delusion We do not know whether it is a grave or a garment.
16-17.translation: What about our delusion? They say that it is by the teams of their own lotus feet. They have flags and other strange red marks, their own feet are like lotus petals, the Vraja-bhuvas, relieving the pain of hooves and hooves, and whose movements are like those of an elephant, whose body is driven by rain, We are the ones in whom the speed of mind and being is offered by that occasion, by the luxurious gaze. The trees of Kuja have lost their destination out of truth [exhaustion] and delusion We do not know whether it is a grave or a garment.

18-19.word_for_word: किं च मणि-धरो मणीन् ग्रथितान् गो-गणनार्थं धरतीति मणि-धरः । — What is more, the jewel-bearer holds the jewels tied together to count the cows.; क्वचिद् देशे एतैर् मणिभिर् गा आसमन्ताद् गणयन् । — In some places, these gems were used to count the cows from the end of the seat.; तथा दयित-गन्धा या तुलसी तस्या मालया सह वर्तमानः । — and the beloved-scented basil, which is present with her garland.; प्रणयिनः प्रियस्यानुचरस्यांसे भुजं प्रक्षिपन् । — The lover threw his arm around the shoulder of his beloved attendant.; यत्र यदा कदाचिद् अगायत । — Wherever and whenever he sang.; तदा क्वणित-वेणु-रवेण वञ्चितान्य् अपहृतानि चित्तानि यासां ताः कृष्णस्य हरिणस्य गृहिण्यो भार्याः गुण-गणार्णं गुण-गण-समुद्रं कृष्णम् अनुगत्य प्राप्य ताः कृष्णम् एवान्वसतान्वासत । — At that time, the wives of the deer, whose minds had been deceived and carried away by the sound of the tinkling flute, followed Kṛṣṇa in the ocean of His virtues and lived there.; न न्यवर्तन्तेत्य् अर्थः । — This means that they do not turn away.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; यतो विमुक्ता गृहाशा याभिस् ता गोपिका इव ता अपि ह्य् एवम् एवान्वासतेति ॥१८.१९॥ — From whom the household hopes of those who have been liberated live like the cowherd women in the same way.
18-19.translation: What is more, the jewel-bearer holds the jewels tied together to count the cows. In some places, these gems were used to count the cows from the end of the seat. and the beloved-scented basil, which is present with her garland. The lover threw his arm around the shoulder of his beloved attendant. Wherever and whenever he sang. At that time, the wives of the deer, whose minds had been deceived and carried away by the sound of the tinkling flute, followed Kṛṣṇa in the ocean of His virtues and lived there. This means that they do not turn away. Where is it from? From whom the household hopes of those who have been liberated live like the cowherd women in the same way.

20-21.word_for_word: तद् एवं वृन्दावन-प्रदेशेषु क्रीडित्वा सायाह्ने गो-धनानि परावर्त्य यमुनायां क्रीडतस् तस्य सौभाग्यम् अनुवर्णयन्ति, कुन्द-दाम-कृत-कौतुक-वेष इति । — That is how they describe his fortune as he played in the regions of Vrindavan and in the evening returned the cows and played in the Yamuna, dressed in a curious dress made of kunda and dam.; गोपीनाम् उत्सवाय कुन्द-दामभिः कृतः कौतुकेनोत्सवेन वेषोऽलङ्कारो येन सः । — The dress and ornaments of the gopīs were curiously made of kunda-damas for their festival.; हे अनघे यशोदे, तव वत्सः पुत्रो नन्द-सूनुः कृष्णः । — O sinless Yaśodā, your calf is Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda.; यद्व सहैव बह्व्यः कथयन्त्यः काश्चित् तव वत्स इति काश्चिन् नन्द-सूनुर् इति चाहुः---नर्म-दो हर्ष-दः सन् यदा विजहार क्रीडति स्म । — At the same time, many people said, “Your calf,” and others called him the son of Nanda.; तदा मलयज-स्पर्शेन मलयजस्य चन्दनस्येव सुरभिः शीतश् च यः स्पर्शस् तेन तं कृष्णं मानयन्न् अनुकूलं यथा तथोपवटि वीजयति । — Then, with the touch of the Malay root, the fragrance and coolness of the Malay root, which is like sandalwood, seeds the upavati as it is favorable to him, honoring him as black.; यद् वा, मलयजो दक्षिणो वयुः । — Or rather, the southern wind born of Malaya.; यद्वा मलयजस्य कृष्णेन स्वङ्गेऽनुलिप्तस्य स्पर्शेन मानयन्न् इति । — In other words, they honored the Malayan by touching his black body.; किं च,वन्दिन इव स्तावकाः सन्तो गन्धर्वादि-गणा वाद्य-गीत-पुष्प-वर्षादिभिः परिवव्रुः परित उपासत ॥२०.२१॥ — Moreover, hosts of gandharvas and other saints worshiped him all around like worshippers with musical instruments songs showers of flowers and so on.
20-21.translation: That is how they describe his fortune as he played in the regions of Vrindavan and in the evening returned the cows and played in the Yamuna, dressed in a curious dress made of kunda and dam. The dress and ornaments of the gopīs were curiously made of kunda-damas for their festival. O sinless Yaśodā, your calf is Kṛṣṇa, the son of Nanda. At the same time, many people said, “Your calf,” and others called him the son of Nanda. Then, with the touch of the Malay root, the fragrance and coolness of the Malay root, which is like sandalwood, seeds the upavati as it is favorable to him, honoring him as black. Or rather, the southern wind born of Malaya. In other words, they honored the Malayan by touching his black body. Moreover, hosts of gandharvas and other saints worshiped him all around like worshippers with musical instruments songs showers of flowers and so on.

22-23.word_for_word: आयान्तम् आलोक्य हृष्यन्त्यः परस्परम् ऊचुः---वत्सलम् इति । — Seeing him coming, they were delighted and said to each other, “It is affectionate.”; व्रजस्य गवां च । — and the cows of Vraja.; यद्वा व्रजे निबद्धानां गवाम् अनुकम्प्यानाम् अस्मकम् इत्य् अर्थः । — Or rather, it means that we are compassionate to the cows that are tied up in Vraja.; वत्सलो हित-कृत् । — affectionate and benevolent.; कुतः ? — Where is it from?; यद् यस्माद् अगध्रः अगं धरतीति गोवर्धनोद्धरणः । — That which is from which the Agadhra, the Agadhra, is the earth, is the lifting of the Govardhana.; बहुशो रक्षणस्योपलक्षणम् एतत् । — This is often a characteristic of protection.; वृद्धैर् ब्रह्मादिभिः । — by the old men, Brahma and others.; पथि वन्द्यमान-चरण इति ते सेर्ष्यं सायं शीघ्रम् आगन्तुं न ददतीत्य् अर्थः । — The worshipful feet on the road mean that they do not allow envy to come early in the evening.; उपोह्य एकी-कृत्य-गीत-युक्तो वेणुर् यस्य सः । — The flute which is used to sing the song of a single act.; श्रम-युक्तयापि कान्त्या नेत्राणां हर्षम् उन्नयन् उच्चैः प्रापयन् । — They raised the joy of their eyes with their exhausting beauty and reached them high.; खुर-रजोभिश् छुरिता व्याप्ताः स्रजो यस्य । — His garlands were covered with the dust of his hooves; सुहृदाम् अस्माकम् आशिषो मनो-रथस्य दित्सया दातुम् इच्छया देवक्य जठरे भवतीति तथा स एवोडु-राजश् चन्द्रो निर्वृति-हेतुत्वेन स एष एतीति ॥२२.२३॥ — It is said that the king of the moon, the moon, is in the womb of Devakī, desiring to bestow the blessings of our friends on the chariot of the mind, and that he is the cause of all happiness.
22-23.translation: Seeing him coming, they were delighted and said to each other, “It is affectionate.” and the cows of Vraja. Or rather, it means that we are compassionate to the cows that are tied up in Vraja. affectionate and benevolent. Where is it from? That which is from which the Agadhra, the Agadhra, is the earth, is the lifting of the Govardhana. This is often a characteristic of protection. by the old men, Brahma and others. The worshipful feet on the road mean that they do not allow envy to come early in the evening. The flute which is used to sing the song of a single act. They raised the joy of their eyes with their exhausting beauty and reached them high. His garlands were covered with the dust of his hooves It is said that the king of the moon, the moon, is in the womb of Devakī, desiring to bestow the blessings of our friends on the chariot of the mind, and that he is the cause of all happiness.

24-25.word_for_word: अतिसम्भ्रमेण काश्चित् समीपम् आयान्तं कथयन्ति--मद-विघूर्णित इति । — In great excitement, some of them say that he is drunk when he comes near.; ईषन् मदेन विघूर्णिते विह्वलिते लोचने यस्य सः । — He whose eyes are slightly distorted by intoxication; बदर-पाण्डु-वदनः ईषत्-पक्व-बदरवत् पाण्डवं वदनं यस्य सः । — Badar-pandu-vadaṇa A person whose face is white like a slightly ripe badar.; अत्र हेतुः--कनक-कुण्डलयोर् लक्ष्म्या कान्त्या मृदु-गण्डौ यस्मिन् तद् वदनं मण्डयन्न् इति । — The reason for this is that the golden earrings adorned the face in which the soft cheeks were adorned with the beauty of Lakshmi.; यद् वा, मृदु कोमलं गण्ड-स्थलं शोभयन्न् इति । — Or rather, they adorn the soft, tender cheekbones.; यदु-पतिर् इति देवकी-जठर-भूर् इति च प्राग् अयं वसुदेवस्य क्वचिज् जातस् तवात्मजः [भा।पु। — Yadu-patir, and Devakī-jathra-bhur, this is your son born somewhere before Vasudeva [Bh.pu.; १०.८.१९] इत्य्-आदि-गर्ग-वाक्य-प्रसिद्ध्योक्तम् । — 10.8.19] It is stated in the famous Garga phrase.; यद् वा, सख उदेयिवान् सात्वतां कुल [भा।पु। — or, the friend who arose in the family of the Sattvas [Bh.p.; १०.३१.४] इतिवत् ज्ञात्वा काश्चिद् वदन्तीति । — 10.31.4] Some say that knowing this.; गजेन्द्र-गतिश् चन्द्र इव प्रसन्न-वक्त्रः । — He moved like an elephant and had a cheerful face like the moon; व्रज-गवाम् अस्माकम् अनन्तं दिन-तापं शमयन्न् उपयाति एष समीपम् आयातीति ॥२४.२५॥ — He comes to us, relieving us of the endless suffering of the day, and says, 'He is coming near.; : न खलु गोपिका-नन्दनो भवान् अखिल-देहिनाम् अन्तरात्म-दृक् । — You are not, indeed, the delight of the cowherd women, but the innermost seer of all embodied beings.; विखनसार्थितो विश्व-गुप्तये सख उदेयिवान् सात्वतां कुले ॥ — My friend, who was requested to dig for the protection of the universe, appeared in the family of the Sātvatas.
24-25.translation: In great excitement, some of them say that he is drunk when he comes near. He whose eyes are slightly distorted by intoxication Badar-pandu-vadaṇa A person whose face is white like a slightly ripe badar. The reason for this is that the golden earrings adorned the face in which the soft cheeks were adorned with the beauty of Lakshmi. Or rather, they adorn the soft, tender cheekbones. Yadu-patir, and Devakī-jathra-bhur, this is your son born somewhere before Vasudeva [Bh.pu. 10.8.19] It is stated in the famous Garga phrase. or, the friend who arose in the family of the Sattvas [Bh.p. 10.31.4] Some say that knowing this. He moved like an elephant and had a cheerful face like the moon He comes to us, relieving us of the endless suffering of the day, and says, 'He is coming near. You are not, indeed, the delight of the cowherd women, but the innermost seer of all embodied beings. My friend, who was requested to dig for the protection of the universe, appeared in the family of the Sātvatas.

26.word_for_word: एवं विरह-दुःखेनापि नु अहो कृष्ण-लीला एव गायन्त्यः तस्मिन् चित्तं चेतना जीवितं यासां ताः । — Thus, even in the pain of separation, oh, those whose minds and consciousness are alive in Him are still singing the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa.; तस्मिन्न् एव मनः संकल्प-रूपं यासां ताः । — Those whose mind is in the form of resolution in that very thing.; अत एव महान् उदय उत्सवो यासां ताः । — That’s why they have a great rise festival.; अहःस्व् अपि रेमिरे ॥२६॥ — They enjoyed themselves for days.
26.translation: Thus, even in the pain of separation, oh, those whose minds and consciousness are alive in Him are still singing the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Those whose mind is in the form of resolution in that very thing. That’s why they have a great rise festival. They enjoyed themselves for days.
